overall: The AG found the Westfield Police Commission violated the Open Meeting Law by posting a notice without its posting time and less than 48 hours before an April 13 meeting; it declined to review an unfiled allegation.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the Commission's April 13 meeting notice did not record the time it was posted.
allegations.key_passage: Here, the notice for the April 13 meeting did not include the time of its posting.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the Commission failed to post notice of the April 13 meeting at least 48 hours in advance, as the notice was posted on a Friday.
allegations.key_passage: Further, because the notice was posted on a Friday, and Saturdays and Sundays are not counted towards the 48-hour notice requirement, we find that it was not posted at least 48 hours prior to the meeting.

allegations.summary: In a request for further review, complainant alleged the Commission failed to convene a meeting to review his complaint; not in the original complaint.
allegations.key_passage: Because this allegation was not included in the complaint filed with the Commission, we decline to review it now.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law.
remedy_passage: We order the Commission's immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law, and we caution that future similar violations may be considered evidence of intent to violate the law.
note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
